user.title: Add a pet
user.description: Each pet lives in its own handheld device on the dashboard's pet shelf. Add the integration again for every extra pet.

data_description.name: Shown on the card and used in entity IDs, for example button.pip_feed. Voice commands use it too.
data_description.world: Sets the device's look and which creatures can hatch. The egg picks one by surprise.
data_description.dashboard: Optional. Tapping this pet's phone notifications opens it, and so does the welcome sent to every phone when the pet is added. Pick a dashboard or type a path, like /lovelace/pets.

reconfigure.title: Rename or move {name}
reconfigure.description: A new name shows on the card and in notifications; entity IDs stay the same. To name a new generation, lay the egg first, then rename it here. A new world changes the device and which creatures hatch. A pet that has already hatched stays where it is, and its next egg starts in the new world.

abort.no_worlds: No pet worlds are ready yet. Reinstall the integration files and try again.

init.title: What {name} notices
init.description: Connect parts of your home to the pet. Every field is optional, and anything you leave empty is ignored. The house never hurts the pet: it only changes its mood, its scene and what it asks for.

sleep.name: Sleep
sleep.description: Lights out always wins. Otherwise the pet goes to bed when the bedtime lights are off and the house is quiet, from an hour before bedtime. If nobody does either, it dozes off on its own an hour after bedtime. The house never wakes it; it wakes at wake time.

data_description.bedtime: It gets drowsy 30 minutes before. Turning lights-out off after bedtime costs a little happiness.
data_description.wake_time: It wakes up on its own at this time.
data_description.bedtime_lights: When all of these are off, it's time for bed. Bedroom lights work well. A light left on late doesn't keep the pet up past its own bedtime.
data_description.motion: Indoor motion, occupancy or presence sensors. Movement in the last 10 minutes means the house isn't quiet yet.

weather.name: Weather and air
weather.description: Rain brings a rainy scene and a blanket request. Sun, snow and fog change its mood. Indoor temperature outside your comfort range makes it shiver or sweat and ask for a blanket or a fan.

data_description.rain: An on/off "it's raining" entity, or a rain rate where anything above 0 means rain. This beats the forecast, which only says what's likely.
data_description.weather: A weather entity. Used for sunny, snow and fog, and for rain when there's no rain sensor.
data_description.indoor_temperature: One temperature sensor in the main living space.
data_description.comfort_low: Below this the pet shivers and asks for a blanket. Never when the fireplace is lit.
data_description.comfort_high: Above this the pet sweats and asks for a fan.
data_description.aqi: An air quality index sensor. Above 100 the pet wears a little mask and stays in. Cosmetic only.
data_description.solar: Only if your weather station reports solar radiation in W/m². 300 or more counts as sunny, more precise than the forecast.

room.name: The pet's room
room.description: The room the pet lives in. Lights still bright after bedtime make it squint; dim evening light makes it cozy. Daylight is never too bright.

data_description.room_lights: Lights in that room, for example the living room. Still on at half brightness or more after bedtime counts as too bright; before bedtime they never do.
data_description.fireplace: Any entity that's on, heating or above 0 when the fire is lit. The pet curls up by it, gets a little happier, and won't ask for a blanket.
data_description.lux: Optional. 100 lx or more after bedtime also counts as too bright.

activity.name: People and activity
activity.description: Someone arriving gets an excited greeting, at most once every 30 minutes. When nobody is home for a while, the pet goes to the sitter's and time stops for it, so it never gets lonely or hungry. Music makes it dance and the TV makes it watch along, each with a small happiness bonus. Ticking off chores on a to-do list earns the pet treats.

data_description.zone: The pet counts the people in this zone. Only people tracked in Home Assistant count.
data_description.away_after: How long the house has to be empty first.
data_description.sitter_settles: On: if the pet was whining for attention when it left (a fake call), the sitter settles it, so it comes home happy. Off: the whine waits for you. Real needs, like hunger, always wait.
data_description.tv: Media players that are TVs. On or playing counts as watching.
data_description.music: Speakers and displays. Playing anything that isn't video counts as music.
data_description.chores: To-do lists. Each item someone ticks off earns the pet a treat (up to 5 a day); it waits if the pet is asleep or away.

sky.name: Sky
sky.description: The full moon makes the pet happy if it's up late, and a new moon is a starry night. Any moon phase sensor works, such as the Moon integration's; or give the lit fraction instead.

data_description.moon_phase: A sensor whose state is the phase, like "full_moon" or "Full Moon".
data_description.moon_illumination: Optional. The lit fraction, 0–1 or a percentage; 97% or more counts as full.
data_description.moon_altitude: Optional. Degrees above the horizon; the moon only counts while it's up.

privacy.name: Privacy
privacy.description: For wall tablets and shared dashboards.

data_description.privacy: On: an empty house shows the pet napping, never at the sitter's, and the pet never names anyone. Off: dashboards show "at the sitter's".

notifications.name: Notifications
notifications.description: Phone notifications go to whoever taps "notify me" on the pet's status screen.

data_description.dashboard: Tapping one of this pet's notifications opens this dashboard. Pick one or type a path, like /lovelace/pets. Empty opens the app as it was.

error.comfort_range: "Too cold below" must be lower than "Too warm above".
error.same_times: Bedtime and wake time can't be the same, or the pet would never sleep.
error.fireplace_temperature: Pick the fireplace's switch, power sensor or climate entity. A temperature sensor is always above 0, so the fire would always look lit.

no_pet.message: No loaded virtual pet matches that pet or config entry.

wrong_guess.message: "{guess}" isn't a guess in that game; try {guesses}.

not_signed_in.message: Only someone signed in can turn their own pet notifications on or off.

fast_forward.name: Fast forward
fast_forward.description: Debug tool: lives through the given number of hours right now, at normal rates. Calls left unanswered in that time count as care misses.

config_entry_id.name: Pet
config_entry_id.description: Which pet. Leave empty for all pets.

notify_me.name: Notify me
notify_me.description: Turns this pet's phone notifications on or off for you, the user calling it. They go to your phones through the Home Assistant app: calls, sickness, hatching, growing up, traits, the season's first snow and frost, and new eggs.

enabled.name: Enabled
enabled.description: On to get notifications, off to stop.

visit.name: Visit
visit.description: Tells the pet that you, the user calling it, looked in. The card calls it when you open it: the first visit of the day counts toward your bond with the pet, and an afternoon visit grants a "come say hi" wish. Counted at most hourly. The response holds what the pet has to tell only you (notes), each once.

my_day.name: My day
my_day.description: Lets the pet notice your day, or stops it, for you, the user calling it: steps, stairs, a bike ride or a run, and a good night's sleep, from the phones you signed in to the Home Assistant app with. It only ever says something when a day stands out for the better, and only to you. The closer your bond, the more it notices.

enabled.name: Enabled
enabled.description: On to let it notice your day, off to stop.

play_game.name: Play a game
play_game.description: One round of a game the card's play button starts. Five rounds make a game; three right guesses win it. Left or right: the pet hides left or right and you guess; the first guess starts a game. Higher or lower: call once without a guess to start and see the first number (1-9), then guess whether the next is higher or lower.

guess.name: Guess
guess.description: Left or right; lower or higher. Leave it out to start a game.

share_news.name: Share news
share_news.description: Tells the pet a bit of news, and it says it in its speech bubble on the card ('did you hear? ...'). Cosmetic only: no stat changes. Dropped while the pet is asleep, away or still an egg, and at most one bit of news shows every 30 minutes per pet.

entity_id.name: Pet
entity_id.description: Any entity of the pet. Pick several for several pets.

headline.name: Headline
headline.description: What the pet says. Extra spaces are tidied away and anything past 60 characters is cut at a word.

topic.name: Topic
topic.description: Optional short label, such as the feed's name (up to 20 characters).

missing_entities.title: {pet} is listening for entities that are gone
missing_entities.description:
{pet}'s settings mention entities that no longer exist in Home Assistant, probably because they were renamed or removed: {entities}.

The pet ignores them, so nothing breaks, but it misses that part of your house. Open Settings → Devices & services → Virtual Pet → the gear next to {pet}, and pick the new entities or clear those fields. This warning goes away once the settings are saved.

world_not_ready.title: {pet}'s world has no creatures yet
world_not_ready.description: {pet} lives in {world}, but none of that world's creatures are installed and ready, so its egg can't hatch. It stays an egg, safe and frozen in place, until they are. Reinstall or update the integration's files; if this keeps happening, please report it.

save_damaged.title: {pet}'s save file was damaged
save_damaged.description: Part of {pet}'s save file couldn't be read. {pet} kept its name, family, journal, memories and bonds where they could be read, and started the rest fresh. The file as it was is kept as `.storage/{backup}`. To go back to it: stop Home Assistant, fix the file, rename it to `.storage/virtual_pet.{entry_id}`, and start Home Assistant again.

save_damaged_egg.title: {pet}'s save file was damaged
save_damaged_egg.description: {pet}'s save file couldn't be read at all, so {pet} started again as an egg. The file as it was is kept as `.storage/{backup}` (Home Assistant names an unreadable file `….corrupt.<time>`). To go back to it: stop Home Assistant, fix the file, rename it to `.storage/virtual_pet.{entry_id}`, and start Home Assistant again.

people_damaged.title: The pets' memories of people were damaged
people_damaged.description: The file where the pets keep what they know about each person (birthdays, answers, settings) couldn't be read, so they start fresh with everyone. Your pets and your bonds with them are fine. The file as it was is kept as `.storage/{backup}`. To go back to it: stop Home Assistant, fix the file, rename it to `.storage/virtual_pet.people`, and start Home Assistant again.
